gen-gf-turret-road-gf-ibm-plex-sans-jp: Rounded, ruler-straight and loud: Turret Road bends like a bracket, while IBM Plex Sans JP finishes each curve in a clean gap. Long paragraphs in it would flow quietly, with little contrast between strokes.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-ibm-plex-sans-kr: Rounded and loud, Turret Road keeps its rounds and stems in a single weight. IBM Plex Sans KR leaves every curve end open, which keeps lengthy text moving easily.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-k2d: Smooth tube-like strokes hold through every bend, with c terminals hanging far from the bowl. K2D does best at running text, while Turret Road does best at bold, round display lines.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-kodchasan: Turret Road draws round, bracket-like letters in a constant weight, loud from across the room. Kodchasan hangs its terminals open and skips calligraphic thinning, so extended reading stays smooth.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-kumbh-sans: Kumbh Sans cuts its terminals short of the bowl, in fixed-pen strokes. Beneath the round, loud headings of Turret Road, that fixed-pen body keeps quiet and lets the display letters do the shouting.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-lato: Lato sweeps its s curves wide and barely curls them in, giving the sans a relaxed look. Turret Road has no hairlines to squint at, and Lato carries a page of text without tiring the eye.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-line-seed-jp: Turret Road draws loud, round letters with one constant line weight from curve to stem. And LINE Seed JP, a sans with horizontals matching its verticals, gives the eye open counters to slip through below.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-livvic: Livvic curves without stress and opens its c generously. Turret Road brings loud, round, bracket-shaped letters in a constant weight at the top, and Livvic murmurs back, friendly and clean.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-m-plus-1p: Turret Road looks like a single wire bent into round letters. The standout quality is how M PLUS 1p leaves every curve end open beneath that bent-wire boldness, giving the text room.
gen-gf-turret-road-gf-m-plus-code-latin: Round, bracket-like curves in a constant weight give Turret Road its commanding look, while M PLUS Code Latin bends neon-tube strokes. One commands while the other pours out wide, pitcher-mouthed c shapes.
